this work shows the possibility of using a fleet of AUVs for adaptive sampling of the CTD environment, using a leader-follower formation with a real-time unsupervised learning algorithm that updates a GMM in real-time, and that uses the variational error distance to reconfigure the AUVs formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing the use of an adaptive sampling strategy based on a coordinated fleet of AUVs that use an unsupervised learning technique to model the CFD data that they are acquiring in real-time.

we have developed a real-time adaptive sampling system for a fleet of AUVs that uses a GMM unsupervised learning algorithm to model the CDT data and a variational error to compute the distance between the followers and the leader.

we have developed a novel adaptive sampling strategy for AUVs that is based on the use of GMMs to represent and learn the CTD data and that uses the variational distance to compute a notion of error between the GMM of each AUV and the GMM of the leader, and that is used to scale the formation of AUVs in order to improve their efficiency in a given region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of an unsupervised learning algorithm in the context of adaptive sampling is a promising approach to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the sampling process.
, by using a simple GMM-based algorithm, it is possible to achieve adaptive sampling in a coordinated fleet of AUVs in a real-time manner.
the proposed adaptive sampling algorithm is robust to the initial conditions of the GMMs, and it is able to improve the efficiency and the accuracy of the CTD measurements.
